## Statement · **draft**
Let $G$ be a group and $S \subseteq G$. The set

$$C_G(S) := \{\, g \in G : g s = s g \ \text{for all}\ s \in S \,\} \le G$$

is the **centralizer** of $S$ in $G$; put $C_G(x) := C_G(\{x\})$, with the convention $C_G(\emptyset) = G$.

$C_G(S)$ is a subgroup. $C_G(G) = Z(G)$ is the **center** of $G$. Under the conjugation action $g \cdot x = gxg^{-1}$, the subgroup $C_G(x)$ is exactly the stabilizer of $x$.
